subject: Prompt-pack validation: triage matrix & escalation runway
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Sara Lee <sara.lee@acme-retail.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-11-22T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Prompt-pack validation: triage matrix & escalation runway

Team —

Quick note to align before the prompt-pack A/B starts next week (Nov 29). Acme is piloting three prompt variants for their shopper-assist flow; we need a short, operational triage matrix that defines: acceptance thresholds, regression gates, and an escalation runway (who we call and what action to take at each signal).

Attachments: promptpack_v1_spec.pdf (spec + test cases), eval-cases.csv (sample prompts + expected signals)

High-level asks:
- Product: confirm primary evaluation metric (we currently have NPS-like satisfaction and a model-confidence fallback).
- ML/Evals: propose thresholds for green/yellow/red and what per-metric delta triggers rollback.
- Eng (ops): confirm acceptable rollback latency and who owns the runbook steps.

My proposal (quick first pass):
- Primary metric: inline satisfaction score (Acme rubric) — require >= +3% absolute uplift at 95% CI for promotion.
- Regression guard: any segment drop > 2% absolute on core conversion OR increase in PII-extraction false positives > 0.5% => immediate pause and canary to baseline.
- Rollback runway: 30 minutes to revert model variant; ops page must include doc link + escalation list.

Please review and add edits inline in the doc link. If we can land owners by EOD tomorrow I’ll push the mutual action plan to Acme.

Thanks,
Aditya
Aditya Rao
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference
---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Sara Lee <sara.lee@acme-retail.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-11-22T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Prompt-pack validation: triage matrix & escalation runway

Thanks Aditya — good framing. A few clarifying points from the eval side: 

- Metric set: can we use a primary "helpfulness lift" metric (binary converted from Acme survey) + secondary safety metric (hallucination / PII flags)? The team already has instrumentation for both.
- Thresholds: suggest green >= +2.5% absolute helpfulness (stable across 3 days of traffic), yellow between +1% and +2.5% (requires side-by-side review), red <= +1% or any statistically significant safety regression.
- Statistical rules: use sequential testing with early-stopping for large effects; require 95% CI for promotion.

Operational asks for engineering: what is the expected cold-start impact for a variant flip (latency/regression to baseline state)? If rollback takes >10m we should tighten the emergency pause thresholds.

I added comments in the doc and attached a small CSV with the target eval cases.

- Marissa
Senior Product Manager, Evals

Date: 2026-11-23T08:29:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Prompt-pack validation: triage matrix & escalation runway

Looping Rohan for ops posture. A couple of operational constraints from our side: 

- Rollback runway: realistic worst-case to switch variants and validate traffic routing back to baseline is ~25–40 minutes depending on KV warmup for the shopper flow. That pushes me toward Marissa's tighter thresholds (so we don't need an urgent revert for marginal dips).
- Canary plan: recommend a 1% traffic canary for 3 hours with automated health checks (latency, error rate, primary metric). If green, expand to 10% for 24h, then full ramp.
- On-call: Rohan (rohan@redwood.ai) will be the primary for the launch window; escalation list is: Rohan -> Eng TL (Connor O'Brien) -> Aditya. Please confirm pager routing and make sure runbook steps are present in rollback-checklist.md.

I created a short rollback-checklist.md (attached) with exact CLI commands and the verification queries we run post-flip. Also flagged a known warmup caveat for cached prefix states — we should document that in the playbook so Acme knows the expected transient behavior.

Grace
Director, Product Reliability

- We accept the proposed staged canary (1% -> 10% -> 100%) and the green/yellow/red bands Marissa suggested.
- We need the rollback-checklist.md in our shared drive and a 24h window where an Acme engineer and your on-call can do a joint flip for the final ramp. Can we schedule that for Nov 29, 09:00 PST?
- Related asks: please include in the doc the expected user-visible transient states (we'll communicate to PMs and store ops).

I'll upload the PO-approved mutual action plan to the shared folder and assign owners on our side.

Regards,
